reasoning_traces.think:
The core operators define a probabilistic spatial inference system where shot outcomes are mapped through gridded zones and conditioned on goalkeeper dynamics. Shot location probability (P_goal) is derived from spatial partitioning and assigned to discrete zones. Goalkeeper save probability (P_save) is computed using positional relationships and monotonic dependency graphs. These two primitives form a dual structure: one encodes shot likelihood, the other encodes defensive counteraction. The monotonic constraint model ensures that increasing distance or decreasing angle consistently reduce goal probability and increase save probability respectively. Failure modes arise when spatial assumptions break down—such as extreme angles or off-grid shots—and when positional data becomes stale or misaligned with model training. The system's robustness hinges on maintaining consistent feature ordering and updating internal representations with new telemetry.
